title: GPT-6 Astra Designs First FPRAS for Mixed Volumes, Disproving Gurvits’s 2009 Conjecture
whyItMatters: GPT-6 Astra generated the core algorithmic ideas for the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme for mixed volumes of arbitrary convex bodies, disproving Gurvits’s 2009 conjecture.
summary: On November 1, 2026, Xiaoyu Chen and Kuikui Liu (MIT) posted arXiv:2611.01368 presenting the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme (FPRAS) to estimate the mixed volume of n arbitrary compact convex sets in R^n given by weak membership oracles. This resolves a 17-year-old problem in convex geometry and theoretical computer science by disproving Gurvits’s 2009 conjecture that no general FPRAS exists. The authors include a stark AI disclosure in the abstract: "The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm." The algorithm chains a sequence of reductions: normalizing exponentially skewed body scales via a dual maximum-entropy convex program (the Gurvits capacity), well-rounding via global affine transformation of a perturbed Minkowski sum, smoothing nonsmooth bodies via convolution, and reducing smooth well-rounded instances via MCMC to mixed-discriminant approximation.
technicalHighlights: Constructs the first FPRAS for estimating the mixed volume of n arbitrary compact convex bodies in R^n under weak membership oracles, disproving Gurvits’s 2009 conjecture.
Authors explicitly disclose in the abstract that the main algorithmic ideas were generated entirely by GPT-6 Astra, with human authors writing the exposition and proof verification.
Combines Gurvits-capacity convex programming for scale normalization, global affine rounding, convolution smoothing, and MCMC reduction to mixed discriminants.
caveats: Preprint under active community review; the theoretical polynomial exponent is astronomically large (non-practical), leaving a genuinely fast FPRAS as an open problem.

scoreRationale.foundational: Refutes a prominent 17-year-old hardness conjecture in algorithmic convex geometry and establishes polynomial-time approximability of general mixed volumes.
scoreRationale.ripple: Connects convex programming, capacity scaling, and MCMC sampling across algebraic root counting, combinatorics, and geometric algorithms.
scoreRationale.verification: Complete human-vetted mathematical exposition published on arXiv by MIT theoretical computer scientists; formal peer review is pending.
scoreRationale.velocity: GPT-6 Astra autonomously originated the entire reduction architecture resolving a 17-year-old open conjecture.
